back: A friendly understanding that settles disputes between states, without a binding promise to fight for each other.
Wilhelm II's 'world policy' from the late 1890s: colonies, influence and a big navy to make Germany a world power.

front: Who was in the Triple Alliance (1882)?
Who was in the Triple Entente, and when was it completed?
back: Britain, France and Russia; completed by the Anglo-Russian Entente of 1907.

front: When was the Anglo-Japanese Alliance signed?
What was HMS Dreadnought, and when was it launched?
back: A revolutionary British battleship launched in 1906 that made older battleships out of date.

front: When did the Franco-Russian Alliance come into force?
back: 1894, after Germany let its Reinsurance Treaty with Russia lapse in 1890.

front: Why did the Schlieffen Plan make a crisis harder to control?
back: It required Germany to attack France quickly through Belgium as soon as Russia mobilised, so a war with Russia became a war with France too.

front: Give two reasons why the alliances may have made war LESS likely.
back: They were defensive and deterred attack; they did not force members to fight (Italy stayed neutral in 1914; Britain had no binding promise).
